## Assumptions

- Each candidate bank uses \(N\) identical capacitors, so ripple current divides equally, consistent with the manual’s parallel-bank equations.
- Catalogue capacitance, ESR, and thermal resistance are nominal; no unstated tolerances or aging allowances are applied.
- The voltage peak is defined by the manual as \(V_{\text{pk}}=V_{\text{DC,nom}}+\Delta V_{\text{overshoot}}\). Carrier ripple is checked separately.
- Bank cost is the sum of capacitor unit costs.

## 1. Altitude voltage derating

At \(H=12000\text{ m}\),

\[
C_{\text{alt},V}
=1.000-0.015\left(\frac{12000-3000}{1000}\right)
=1-0.015(9)
=0.865
\]

The repetitive peak operating voltage is

\[
V_{\text{pk}}=900+135=1035\text{ V}
\]

| Model | Derated working voltage \(V_{\text{NDC}}C_{\text{alt},V}\) | Voltage result |
|---|---:|---|
| EPC-1100-80 | \(1100(0.865)=951.50\text{ V}\) | Fails: \(951.5<1035\) |
| EPC-1200-60 | \(1200(0.865)=1038.00\text{ V}\) | Passes |
| EPC-1250-80 | \(1250(0.865)=1081.25\text{ V}\) | Passes |

Thus, EPC-1100-80 is infeasible regardless of the number of parallel units.

## 2. Frequency-weighted ripple current

Using the exact table values

\[
K_f(1.2\text{ kHz})=\frac57,\qquad
K_f(40\text{ kHz})=\frac56
\]

the total effective ripple current referred to \(10\text{ kHz}\) is

\[
\begin{aligned}
I_{\text{eff,total}}
&=\sqrt{\left(\frac{90}{5/7}\right)^2+
         \left(\frac{140}{5/6}\right)^2}\\
&=\sqrt{126^2+168^2}\\
&=\sqrt{44100}\\
&=210\text{ A}_{\text{rms}}
\end{aligned}
\]

For \(N\) identical capacitors,

\[
I_{\text{eff,unit}}=\frac{210}{N}
\]

The catalogue \(10\text{ kHz}\) ripple-current screen requires:

- EPC-1200-60:

\[
N\ge \frac{210}{62.5}=3.36
\quad\Rightarrow\quad N\ge4
\]

- EPC-1250-80:

\[
N\ge \frac{210}{82.2}=2.5547
\quad\Rightarrow\quad N\ge3
\]

## 3. Capacitance requirement

- EPC-1200-60:

\[
N\ge \frac{220}{60}=3.6667
\quad\Rightarrow\quad N\ge4
\]

- EPC-1250-80:

\[
N\ge \frac{220}{80}=2.75
\quad\Rightarrow\quad N\ge3
\]

## 4. High-altitude thermal requirement

At \(12000\text{ m}\),

\[
M_{\text{alt,th}}=1.620
\]

The allowable temperature rise is

\[
\Delta T_{\max}=105-65=40\text{ K}
\]

### EPC-1200-60

\[
R_{\text{th,eff}}=5.685(1.620)=9.2097\text{ K/W}
\]

\[
\begin{aligned}
T_{\text{core}}
&=65+\left(\frac{210}{N}\right)^2(0.00180)(9.2097)\\
&=65+\frac{731.065986}{N^2}
\end{aligned}
\]

Therefore,

\[
\frac{731.065986}{N^2}\le40
\]

\[
N\ge\sqrt{\frac{731.065986}{40}}
=4.2751
\quad\Rightarrow\quad N\ge5
\]

Check:

\[
T_{\text{core}}(N=4)=110.69^\circ\text{C}\quad\text{(fails)}
\]

\[
T_{\text{core}}(N=5)=94.24^\circ\text{C}\quad\text{(passes)}
\]

### EPC-1250-80

\[
R_{\text{th,eff}}=4.38(1.620)=7.0956\text{ K/W}
\]

\[
\begin{aligned}
T_{\text{core}}
&=65+\left(\frac{210}{N}\right)^2(0.00135)(7.0956)\\
&=65+\frac{422.436546}{N^2}
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus,

\[
N\ge\sqrt{\frac{422.436546}{40}}
=3.2498
\quad\Rightarrow\quad N\ge4
\]

Check:

\[
T_{\text{core}}(N=3)=111.94^\circ\text{C}\quad\text{(fails)}
\]

\[
T_{\text{core}}(N=4)=91.40^\circ\text{C}\quad\text{(passes)}
\]

## 5. Carrier-frequency voltage ripple

Because \(C_{\text{total}}=NC_{\text{unit}}\), the ripple expression can be written as

\[
\Delta V_{\text{pp}}
=
\frac{1}{N}
\left[
\frac{\sqrt3 I_c}{4f_cC_{\text{unit}}}
+
2\sqrt3 I_c\operatorname{ESR}(40\text{ kHz})
\right]
\]

### EPC-1200-60

\[
\operatorname{ESR}(40\text{ kHz})
=
\frac{1.80\text{ m}\Omega}{(5/6)^2}
=2.592\text{ m}\Omega
\]

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta V_{\text{pp}}
&=\frac{1}{N}\left[
\frac{\sqrt3(140)}{4(40000)(60\times10^{-6})}
+2\sqrt3(140)(0.002592)
\right]\\
&=\frac{26.516127}{N}
\end{aligned}
\]

Hence,

\[
N\ge\frac{26.516127}{12}=2.2097
\quad\Rightarrow\quad N\ge3
\]

At the thermally required \(N=5\),

\[
\Delta V_{\text{pp}}=\frac{26.516127}{5}
=5.3032\text{ V}<12\text{ V}
\]

### EPC-1250-80

\[
\operatorname{ESR}(40\text{ kHz})
=
\frac{1.35\text{ m}\Omega}{(5/6)^2}
=1.944\text{ m}\Omega
\]

\[
\Delta V_{\text{pp}}
=\frac{19.887096}{N}
\]

Hence,

\[
N\ge\frac{19.887096}{12}=1.6573
\quad\Rightarrow\quad N\ge2
\]

At the thermally required \(N=4\),

\[
\Delta V_{\text{pp}}=\frac{19.887096}{4}
=4.9718\text{ V}<12\text{ V}
\]

## 6. Minimum feasible bank and cost

| Model | Capacitance minimum | Catalogue ripple minimum | Thermal minimum | Carrier-ripple minimum | Feasible minimum \(N\) | Bank cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| EPC-1100-80 | — | — | — | — | Infeasible voltage | — |
| EPC-1200-60 | 4 | 4 | 5 | 3 | 5 | \(5(130)=\$650\) |
| EPC-1250-80 | 3 | 3 | 4 | 2 | 4 | \(4(185)=\$740\) |

The lowest-cost compliant bank is therefore **five EPC-1200-60 capacitors in parallel**.

For the selected bank:

\[
C_{\text{total}}=5(60)=300\ \mu\text{F}
\]

\[
I_{\text{eff,unit}}=\frac{210}{5}=42.0\text{ A}_{\text{rms}}
\]

\[
P_{\text{loss,unit}}=42^2(0.00180)=3.1752\text{ W}
\]

\[
T_{\text{core}}
=65+3.1752(9.2097)
=94.2426^\circ\text{C}
\]

The selected bank also has \(42.0<62.5\text{ A}_{\text{rms}}\) catalogue effective ripple current and \(5.3032<12.0\text{ V}\) carrier ripple.

### Results

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Bank Configuration | 5 × EPC-1200-60 in parallel |
| Total Bank Cost (USD) | 650 |
| Total Capacitance (µF) | 300 |
| Derated Working Voltage Limit (V) | 1038.0 |
| Peak Operating Voltage (V) | 1035.0 |
| Effective Ripple Current per Capacitor (A_rms) | 42.0 |
| Core Hot-Spot Temp (°C) | 94.24 |

Assumptions used: pressures are absolute as stated; the tabulated \(F_p\) values are used directly because they are pre-certified for a DN150 header with adjacent concentric reducers/expanders; methanol is Newtonian here because \(\nu=0.70\ \text{cSt}<20\ \text{cSt}\); the VES-14 Certification Rule is used for travel, i.e. \(h=512R\) for \(R\le0.050\) and \(h=100R\) for \(R>0.50\).

Common liquid data:

\[
G_f=\frac{790}{1000}=0.790
\]

\[
F_F=0.96-0.28\sqrt{\frac{P_v}{P_c}}
=0.96-0.28\sqrt{\frac{32.0}{8096}}
=0.96-0.28\sqrt{\frac1{253}}
=0.9423965508
\]

At the maximum-flow letdown, \(P_1=1600\ \text{kPa abs}\):

\[
P_1-F_FP_v=1600-(0.9423965508)(32.0)=1569.843310\ \text{kPa}
\]

Maximum-flow sizing point:

\[
\Delta P_{\max}=1600-750=850\ \text{kPa}=8.50\ \text{bar}
\]

\[
\frac{\Delta P}{P_1}=\frac{850}{1600}=0.53125>0.50
\]

so the Multi-Step \(K_m\) penalty applies at maximum flow.

\[
C_{v,0,\max}=
\frac{145}{0.865\sqrt{8.50/0.790}}
=51.104127
\]

Minimum-flow sizing point:

\[
\Delta P_{\min}=1800-1100=700\ \text{kPa}=7.00\ \text{bar}
\]

\[
\frac{\Delta P}{P_1}=\frac{700}{1800}=0.3888889\le0.50
\]

so \(K_m=1.000\) at minimum flow for all trims.

\[
C_{v,0,\min}=
\frac{5.0}{0.865\sqrt{7.00/0.790}}
=1.941862
\]

Screening in ascending mass order:

| Model | Mass (kg) | \(K_m\) at max | \(C_{v,\rm req,max}\) | \(h_{\max}\) (%) | \(h_{\min}\) (%) | \(\Delta P_{ic}\) (kPa) | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| VFC-9080-S | 48.0 | 1.000 | \(51.104127/0.945=54.0784\) | 60.09 | 11.69 | \(0.518(0.945)^2(1569.843310)=726.19\) | Fail: \(850>726.19\) |
| VFC-9080-M | 54.0 | 0.945 | \(51.104127/(0.975\cdot0.945)=55.4651\) | 89.46 | 16.45 | \(0.670(0.975)^2(1569.843310)=999.86\) | Fail: \(h_{\max}>85\%\) |
| VFC-9100-S | 72.0 | 1.000 | \(51.104127/0.967=52.8481\) | 50.85 | 7.34 | \(0.518(0.967)^2(1569.843310)=760.39\) | Fail: \(\Delta P_{ic}\); also \(h_{\min}<10\%\) |
| VFC-9100-M | 79.0 | 0.873 | \(51.104127/(0.964\cdot0.873)=60.7246\) | 75.91 | 12.89 | \(0.730(0.964)^2(1569.843310)=1064.96\) | Pass |

For the selected VFC-9100-M:

\[
C_{v,\rm req,max}=60.7246,\qquad
R_{\max}=\frac{60.7246}{80.0}=0.7590576
\]

\[
h_{\max}=100R_{\max}=75.9058\%\le85\%
\]

\[
C_{v,\rm req,min}=\frac{1.941862}{0.964}=2.014380,\qquad
R_{\min}=\frac{2.014380}{80.0}=0.02517975
\]

\[
h_{\min}=512R_{\min}=12.8920\%\ge10\%
\]

Choked-flow check:

\[
\Delta P_{\rm choked}
=F_L^2F_p^2(P_1-F_FP_v)
=(0.94)^2(0.964)^2(1569.843310)
=1289.04\ \text{kPa}
\]

\[
\Delta P_{\max}=850\ \text{kPa}<1289.04\ \text{kPa}
\]

and also

\[
850\ \text{kPa}\le \Delta P_{ic}=1064.96\ \text{kPa}
\]

Final conclusion: the smallest-mass valve satisfying the capacity, travel, incipient-cavitation, and choked-flow checks is the VFC-9100-M, DN100, mass 79.0 kg. The heavier VFC-9150-M is not needed for minimum mass and, if checked, also gives \(h_{\min}\approx7.95\%<10\%\).

| Results | Selected value |
|---|---:|
| Model | VFC-9100-M |
| Nominal Size DN (mm) | 100 |
| Mass (kg) | 79.0 |
| Piping Geometry Factor Fp | 0.964 |
| Required Cv at Max Flow | 60.72 |
| Travel at Max Flow (%) | 75.91 |
| Travel at Min Flow (%) | 12.89 |
| Allowable Incipient Pressure Drop dP_ic (kPa) | 1064.96 |

## 1. Assumptions and duty factors

- The 85 N·m torque in the constant-speed phase is the total resisting output torque for that phase, not an additional torque added to the 45 N·m friction torque.
- Positive torque is in the direction of conveyor motion.
- No holding torque is required during the dwell.
- Because this is an electric servo in cyclic indexing duty:
  \[
  K_a=1.15
  \]
- One cycle takes 1.00 s, so the indexing frequency is:
  \[
  60\ \text{cycles/min}
  \]
  Therefore, \(C_{\text{duty}}=0.90\).
- At \(40^\circ\text{C}\), \(C_{\text{th}}=0.82\).

## 2. Output torque profile

The maximum output angular speed is

\[
\omega_{\text{out}}
=150\frac{2\pi}{60}
=15.70796\ \text{rad/s}
\]

The acceleration and deceleration magnitude is

\[
\alpha_{\text{out}}
=\frac{15.70796}{0.20}
=78.53982\ \text{rad/s}^2
\]

The output inertial torque is

\[
T_J=J_L\alpha_{\text{out}}
=0.450(78.53982)
=35.34292\ \text{N·m}
\]

### Acceleration

The friction torque opposes acceleration:

\[
T_{\text{acc}}=T_J+45
=35.34292+45
=80.34292\ \text{N·m}
\]

### Constant-speed run

\[
T_{\text{run}}=85.000\ \text{N·m}
\]

### Deceleration

The friction torque assists deceleration. With positive torque defined in the direction of motion,

\[
T_{\text{dec}}-45=-35.34292
\]

so

\[
T_{\text{dec}}=45-35.34292
=9.65708\ \text{N·m}
\]

Thus the actual peak output torque is

\[
T_{\text{peak}}=\max(80.34292,85.000,9.65708)
=85.000\ \text{N·m}
\]

## 3. RMS output torque and thermal screening

The dwell fraction is

\[
\frac{t_{\text{dwell}}}{t_{\text{total}}}
=\frac{0.20}{1.00}
=0.20\le 0.25
\]

Therefore, the dwell must be excluded from the RMS denominator. The active time is

\[
t_{\text{run}}=0.20+0.40+0.20=0.80\ \text{s}
\]

\[
T_{\text{rms}}
=
\sqrt{
\frac{
(80.34292)^2(0.20)
+(85.000)^2(0.40)
+(9.65708)^2(0.20)
}{0.80}
}
\]

\[
T_{\text{rms}}
=
\sqrt{\frac{4199.64872}{0.80}}
=\sqrt{5249.56090}
=72.4539\ \text{N·m}
\]

The combined thermal derating factor is

\[
C_{\text{th}}C_{\text{duty}}
=0.82(0.90)
=0.738
\]

| Model | Mass (kg) | Derated thermal limit \(T_N(0.738)\) | Thermal result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| KGD-75-08 | 4.2 | \(75(0.738)=55.350\) N·m | Fails |
| KGD-90-08 | 6.8 | \(92(0.738)=67.896\) N·m | Fails |
| **KGD-90-10** | **7.0** | \(105(0.738)=77.490\) N·m | **Passes** |
| KGD-115-05 | 11.2 | \(140(0.738)=103.320\) N·m | Passes, but heavier |
| KGD-115-08 | 11.5 | \(175(0.738)=129.150\) N·m | Passes, but heavier |

The two models lighter than KGD-90-10 fail the thermal requirement. In addition, KGD-75-08 has an excessive equivalent radial load:

\[
F_{r,\text{eq},75}
=2400\frac{38+45}{38+25}
=3161.9\ \text{N}>2500\ \text{N}
\]

Therefore, KGD-90-10 is the lightest possible selection, subject to the remaining checks.

## 4. KGD-90-10 verification

### Peak output torque

For KGD-90-10, \(T_{\max}=330\) N·m:

\[
T_{\text{allowable peak}}
=\frac{T_{\max}}{K_a}
=\frac{330}{1.15}
=286.9565\ \text{N·m}
\]

\[
85.000\le286.9565\ \text{N·m}
\]

The peak-torque requirement is satisfied.

### Maximum input speed

\[
n_{\text{in}}=i\,n_{\text{out}}
=10(150)
=1500\ \text{rpm}
\]

\[
1500<4500\ \text{rpm}
\]

The input-speed limit is satisfied.

### Equivalent radial load

For frame 90:

\[
A=45\ \text{mm},\qquad L_{\text{ref}}=30\ \text{mm}
\]

With \(x=45\) mm:

\[
F_{r,\text{eq}}
=2400\frac{45+45}{45+30}
=2400\frac{90}{75}
=2880\ \text{N}
\]

\[
2880\le F_{r,\max}=3600\ \text{N}
\]

The radial-load limit is satisfied.

### Bearing life

The cycle-averaged output speed, including the dwell, is

\[
n_m=
\frac{
\left(\frac{0+150}{2}\right)(0.20)
+150(0.40)
+\left(\frac{150+0}{2}\right)(0.20)
+0(0.20)
}{1.00}
\]

\[
n_m=\frac{15+60+15}{1.00}=90\ \text{rpm}
\]

For frame 90, \(C_r=14200\) N:

\[
L_{10h}
=
\frac{10^6}{60(90)}
\left(
\frac{14200}{2880(1.15)}
\right)^{10/3}
\]

\[
L_{10h}
=
185.1852
\left(4.28744\right)^{10/3}
\approx23710\ \text{h}
\]

\[
23710>15000\ \text{h}
\]

The bearing-life requirement is satisfied.

### Peak motor torque

For KGD-90-10:

\[
J_{\text{motor}}+J_g
=0.00060+0.00798
=0.00858\ \text{kg·m}^2
\]

During acceleration:

\[
T_{m,\text{acc}}
=
\frac{80.34292}{10(0.96)}
+
(0.00858)(10)(78.53982)
\]

\[
T_{m,\text{acc}}
=8.36905+6.73872
=15.10777\ \text{N·m}
\]

During constant-speed operation:

\[
T_{m,\text{run}}
=\frac{85}{10(0.96)}
=8.85417\ \text{N·m}
\]

Using the same signed dynamic relationship during deceleration gives

\[
T_{m,\text{dec}}
=
\frac{9.65708}{10(0.96)}
-(0.00858)(10)(78.53982)
=-5.73277\ \text{N·m}
\]

where the negative sign indicates braking/regeneration. Therefore, the largest absolute motor torque is

\[
T_{m,\text{peak}}=15.10777\ \text{N·m}
\]

\[
15.10777\le18.0\ \text{N·m}
\]

All catalogue, thermal, bearing, speed, and motor-torque requirements are satisfied.

### Results

| Row | Result |
|---|---:|
| Model | **KGD-90-10** |
| Ratio | **10** |
| Mass (kg) | **7.0** |
| Peak Output Torque (N·m) | **85.00** |
| RMS Output Torque (N·m) | **72.45** |
| Derated Thermal Torque Limit (N·m) | **77.49** |
| Equivalent Radial Load (N) | **2880** |
| Bearing Life L10h (h) | **23,710** |
| Peak Motor Torque (N·m) | **15.11** |

Assumptions used: steady state; all 1300 W is rejected to the coolant; negligible heat leak to the sealed bay and no fouling; constant coolant properties as given. A literal transverse side-by-side pair would need 120 mm of active width, while every listed plate has \(W_f=75\) or \(90\) mm, so I use TAN-08’s stated TVC dual-module **series-serpentine** model: Module 1 is upstream, Module 2 is downstream, and the peak is Module 2 referenced to \(T_{\text{out}}\). For each square module, \(W_{\text{mod}}=60\) mm.

Common flow and coolant rise:

\[
Q_v=6.00\ \text{L/min}=1.00\times10^{-4}\ \text{m}^3/\text{s}
\]

\[
\dot m=\rho Q_v=1055(1.00\times10^{-4})=0.1055\ \text{kg/s}
\]

\[
\dot m c_p=0.1055(3450)=363.975\ \text{W/K}
\]

\[
T_{\text{out}}=45.0+\frac{1300}{363.975}
=45.0+3.57167=48.57167^\circ\text{C}
\]

TIM resistance per module:

\[
A_{\text{mod}}=60\text{ mm}\times60\text{ mm}=36.0\ \text{cm}^2
\]

\[
R_{\text{tim}}=\frac{0.120}{36.0}=0.00333333\ \text{K/W}
\]

\[
P_{\text{mod}}R_{\text{tim}}=650(0.00333333)=2.16667\ \text{K}
\]

Hydraulic correction:

\[
\nu=\frac{\mu}{\rho}=\frac{0.00210}{1055}
=1.99052\times10^{-6}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}
\]

\[
\left(\frac{\nu}{\nu_{\text{ref}}}\right)^{0.25}
=
\left(\frac{1.99052\times10^{-6}}{0.890\times10^{-6}}\right)^{0.25}
=1.22291
\]

\[
\frac{\rho}{\rho_{\text{ref}}}=\frac{1055}{997}=1.0581745
\]

\[
6.00^{1.75}=23.00195,\qquad 
\Delta P_{\text{core}}
=K_{\text{hyd}}(1.0581745)(1.22291)(23.00195)
=29.7657K_{\text{hyd}}\ \text{kPa}
\]

\[
\Delta P_{\text{port}}
=K_{\text{port}}\left(\frac{1055}{1000}\right)6.00^2
=37.98K_{\text{port}}\ \text{kPa}
\]

Thermal multipliers:

\[
F_{\text{gly}}=1.28
\]

For \(W_f=90\) mm:

\[
M_s=\left(\frac{90}{60}\right)^{0.35}=1.152476,\qquad M_sF_{\text{gly}}=1.475169
\]

For \(W_f=75\) mm:

\[
M_s=\left(\frac{75}{60}\right)^{0.35}=1.081231,\qquad M_sF_{\text{gly}}=1.383976
\]

\[
T_{b,\max}=48.57167+650\left(R_{\text{tim}}+R_{\text{th,cat}}M_sF_{\text{gly}}\right)
\]

Screening all catalogue models:

| Model | Mass (kg) | \(v_{\text{ch}}\) (m/s) | \(\Delta P_{\text{total}}\) (kPa) | \(T_{b,\max}\) (°C) | Decision |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| TVC-180-AL | 1.15 | 2.3810 | 41.2772 | 98.6813 | Fail: velocity, pressure, temperature |
| TVC-200-AL | 1.45 | 1.8519 | 32.8924 | 97.2431 | Fail: \(T_{b,\max}>95.0^\circ\text{C}\) |
| TVC-250-AL | 1.85 | 1.5625 | 35.6473 | 91.3096 | Pass |
| TVC-220-CU | 2.60 | 2.0833 | 39.8966 | 86.2719 | Fail: \(\Delta P>38.0\) kPa |
| TVC-260-CU | 3.10 | 1.6667 | 31.5879 | 84.9225 | Pass |

Final selection: **TVC-250-AL**. It is the lightest plate satisfying the erosion-velocity limit, the 38.0 kPa corrected pressure-drop limit, and the 95.0 °C peak-baseplate limit. The lighter TVC-200-AL fails thermally, and TVC-220-CU fails on pressure drop.
